sessions.phase_label: Landing-page design, responsive handoff, and initial deployment
Website refinements, access pages, and Console design

requirements.title: Landing-Page Hero Presentation
requirements.definition: The landing page must present the company through a polished hero section with an approved composition, headline treatment, background, and supporting product imagery.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the hero's composition and presentation; exact cross-site typography/color tokens, responsive breakpoint behavior, and CTA behavior are owned by separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Primary Sign-Up Action
requirements.definition: The landing page must prominently expose a primary action through which visitors can begin signing up for the service.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the primary sign-up CTA and its prominence, not the unconfirmed optional contact form or possible pricing inquiry content.

requirements.title: Landing-Page Content Sequence
requirements.definition: The landing page must organize its post-hero content around a concise visitor-oriented sequence, including an explanation of how the service works.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns section ordering and the How It Works content mechanism; it excludes hero composition, footer content, and site navigation.

requirements.title: Website Design Tokens
requirements.definition: The website implementation must be supported by defined typography, color, spacing, border, radius, content-width, and interaction-state values together with the required font assets.
requirements.boundary_note: Treats token values and font assets as parameters of one reusable website design system rather than separate Requirements for each color, font, or spacing value.

requirements.title: Website Implementation Handoff
requirements.definition: Website designs and assets must be handed off in a form suitable for implementation using plain HTML and Tailwind CSS.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the implementation-compatible source and asset package, not the independently evolving visual requirements represented by those files.

requirements.title: Website Responsive Behavior
requirements.definition: Website layouts must adapt coherently across desktop, tablet, mobile, and intermediate viewport widths without overlapping or unusable content.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns breakpoint and adaptive-layout behavior across viewports; visual content, navigation, and footer decisions remain separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Website Header Navigation
requirements.definition: The website header must expose only the navigation structure appropriate to the current site content and available pages.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers header navigation presence and structure, including its removal from the short landing page and later reintroduction as additional pages become available.

requirements.title: Website Footer
requirements.definition: The website must provide a responsive footer with approved company details, page links, social links, copyright information, and visual treatment.
requirements.boundary_note: Footer content, responsive layout, and background treatment form one reusable page-chrome mechanism; header navigation and general page themes remain separate.

requirements.title: Shared Website Page Treatment
requirements.definition: Follow-on website pages must maintain a coherent visual relationship to the landing page through a shared page treatment and consistent site-level styling.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers site-wide visual continuity and page treatment, not the content of individual pages or the independently specified Sign In and Provisioning experiences.

requirements.title: Sign-In Page Styling
requirements.definition: The AWS Cognito-generated sign-in experience must be visually styled and branded for Actia, including an appropriate page background.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers branding and visual presentation of the Cognito sign-in page, not authentication functionality or the separate provisioning wizard.

requirements.title: Account Provisioning Wizard Styling
requirements.definition: The account provisioning wizard must receive a branded, responsive visual treatment with defined layout, progress-node, control-state, and background styling.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the wizard's visual shell and interaction styling; the client's underlying provisioning logic and workflow implementation are excluded.

requirements.title: Console Shell Visual Style
requirements.definition: The Console shell and main canvas must have a coherent branded style for its header, navigation container, footer, typography, colors, icons, and light and dark themes.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the shared visual shell as a tightly coupled mechanism; side-panel information architecture and button styling have distinct decision trajectories and are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Console Navigation Structure
requirements.definition: Console-level and application-level navigation must be organized without visually competing side panels, using an agreed collapsible or nested navigation structure.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns the placement and nesting behavior of Console and application navigation, not the general shell appearance or individual application content.

requirements.title: Console Button Style
requirements.definition: Console buttons must use an agreed branded treatment for color, shape, size, corner style, and optional icon use.
requirements.boundary_note: Button properties are parameters of one control-style mechanism and are separated from the broader shell because they receive their own explicit design decision and implementation trajectory.

requirements.title: Platform Communication Diagram
requirements.definition: The platform solution page must include a production-ready diagram showing customer and staff communication channels with appropriate labels.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the communication-channel diagram and its customer/staff labels; the separate cyclical agent diagram has different content and acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Agent Cycle Diagram
requirements.definition: The agent solution page must include a production-ready cycle diagram whose directional flow is shown clockwise.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separate from the platform communication diagram because it represents a different concept and has an independent directional-flow requirement.

unresolved_candidates.description: A bottom contact form and possible pricing inquiry are proposed, but the supplied history does not show a clear client decision establishing either as a retained independent Requirement.
Product or dashboard imagery is discussed as a placeholder and possible direction, but it is unclear whether a specific independently required preview asset was confirmed.
The client asks whether the brand guide should be updated with implementation details, but no clear decision establishes a separate brand-guide revision deliverable.
The need for a non-competing Console navigation structure is established, but the final panel side and whether nested navigation is accepted remain unresolved.

The proposed design scope covering only login and the post-configuration dashboard is not directly answered; later evidence supports separate Sign In, Provisioning, and Console Requirements but not a final end-to-end flow-design scope.
